newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SAKIC HAT TRICK HELPS AVALANCHE BEAT PENGUINS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SAKIC HAT TRICK HELPS AVALANCHE BEAT PENGUINS.

text.p: Joe Sakic recorded his first hat trick in nearly five years, helping the Colorado Avalanche rally for a 6-3 victory over Pittsburgh and spoiling a landmark effort by Penguins winger Joe Mullen Friday.
Peter Forsberg added a goal and two assists for Colorado, which ended a season-high three-game winless streak.

Mullen scored late in the second period to become the first American-born player in NHL history to reach the 500-goal mark. His teammates came off the bench to congratulate him for a goal that also put Pittsburgh ahead 3-2.

"It's great to get this thing over with, a big relief," Mullen said. "Unfortunately, the lead did not hold up. Everyone just kept telling me to get to the net, get to the net and I was able to tap it in. It's a great thrill, it's been a long season and it's great to get it over with."

But Sakic got a power-play goal with 12 seconds to go in the period and added another in a three-goal third period to complete his first hat trick since he scored four times for Quebec on April 14, 1992.
Fredrik Olausson had a goal and an assist for the Penguins, who are winless in their last seven road games and 1-6-3 in their last 10 overall.
Olausson's power-play tally was the only scoring in the first period. Colorado goaltender Patrick Roy kept his team in the game by stopping Ron Francis on a breakaway.
Francis beat Roy 90 seconds into the second to give Pittsburgh a two-goal cushion, but Sakic answered at 9:03 and Forsberg tied it at 14:58.
Mullen got his milestone goal with 3:59 to go in the period, tapping in Alex Hicks' shot for his fifth of the season. The New York City native is the 25th 500-goal scorer in NHL history.
"We played with patience and composure tonight," Avalanche coach Marc Crawford said. "Patrick made a big save for us. Even though we got behind, we still had great chances."

In Anaheim, Joe Murphy ended a long drought by scoring with 3:42 left in regulation, enabling the St. Louis Blues to salvage a 4-4 tie with the Mighty Ducks, who extended their unbeaten streak to a club-record 10 games (6-0-4).

Murphy took a cross-ice pass from Pierre Turgeon and put a wrist shot from the right side of the slot into the lower right corner of the net. It was the 15th goal of the season and first since January 29 for Murphy.

Brett Hull added his 40th goal and two assists for the Blues, who are unbeaten in their last three games (2-0-1) but fell into a tie with Phoenix and Edmonton for fourth place in the Western Conference.
The Ducks are seventh in the West, one point behind the Blues, Coyotes and Oilers.
In Ottawa, Niklas Sundstrom scored 84 seconds into overtime and Adam Graves recorded his first hat trick in more than two years as the New York Rangers continued their mastery over the Senators, 4-3.

Sundstrom's slap shot from the top of the left faceoff circle beat goaltender Ron Tugnutt to the stick side for his 23rd goal of the season. It was his third game-winner and second overtime tally in six games.
The goal came moments after teammate Wayne Gretzky put a backhander wide of the net on a partial breakaway and Tugnutt scrambled to make a glove save on a shot from the point.
New York improved its all-time mark against the Senators to 15-2, including an 8-1 record in Ottawa.

In Phoenix, Nikolai Khabibulin stopped 26 shots in his 30th straight start and Jeremy Roenick scored a goal and set up another as the Coyotes posted their fourth straight road victory, 4-1 over the reeling San Jose Sharks.
Dallas Drake and Shane Doan added second-period goals and Keith Tkachuk added an empty-net goal for Phoenix, 4-1-1 in its last six games.
Tony Granato had the lone goal for San Jose, which has lost five of its last six games. The Sharks are 13 points out of the final playoff spot with 14 games remaining.
In Dallas, Mike Modano's second goal of the game with 3:37 left in regulation lifted the surging Stars into a 4-4 tie with the Chicago Blackhawks.
Jim Cummins scored at 2:01 of the third period and Bob Probert tallied with 5:03 left to give Chicago a 4-3 lead.
But Modano tied it 86 seconds later with his 30th of the season. His wrist shot from the left faceoff circle bounced in front of goaltender Chris Terreri and carried into the net.
Benoit Hogue and Joe Nieuwendyk also scored and Darryl Sydor had two assists for the Stars, 2-0-2 in their last four games.
